Without a fundamental business turnaround or governance catalyst, these names are destined to revert to values reflective of their eroding margins and heavy debt burdens [D01, D02, D05].

final.what_would_change_our_mind: A fundamental shift in the underlying business model that creates a durable, cash-generative path not dependent on short-term retail technicals, accompanied by a clear governance path to unlock value.
final.memo:
The companies represent classic examples of businesses facing severe secular decline, currently being pushed to irrational valuations by a retail-driven short squeeze [D01, D05]. The disconnect between the current market capitalization of ~$24.24 billion and the fundamental realities of their operations is stark [D04].

When we look at the math, the videogame retailer generated -6.2% operating margins in FY2019, while the cinema operator continues to suffer from public-health and release-schedule headwinds [D02, D05]. Comparing the cinema operator to healthy peers reveals a wide margin gap, with its 2.5% margin lagging significantly behind the 10.3% reported by Cinemark and 19.5% by IMAX [D02, D06].

The market is currently ignoring the structural threats posed by digital distribution and the precedence of senior lease obligations over common equity [D01, D05]. We see no fundamental catalyst for value creation, as the recent financing and equity issuance programs are merely stop-gap measures for companies in terminal states [D01, D02, D03].

We pass on this situation entirely [D01, D05]. We prefer to allocate capital to event-driven situations where we have a measurable edge, not to speculative, technical-driven volatility that lacks a fundamental floor [D01, D05].
